title: From harmonic to sound-like oscillations in a quantum gas confined in a gravity compensated shell trap
authors: Matthieu Cassus, Rishabh Sharma, Maxime Pesche, Laurent Longchambon, Thomas Badr, Romain Dubessy, Hélène Perrin
abstract: We study the center of mass oscillations of a quantum gas in a shell shaped trap in the presence of a vertical force opposed to gravity. The measured harmonic frequency at the bottom of the shell is compared with an analytical formula for the trap potential including corrections beyond the rotating wave approximation. When gravity is partially compensated, a quartic correction to the harmonic motion has to be included due to the shell curvature. As gravity is nearly canceled, the quantum gas occupies a large fraction of the lower hemisphere. Driving the center of mass induces internal excitations in the quantum gas, whose time evolution is governed by the presence of sound waves. Relaxation processes induce a strong damping of the center of mass oscillation in this limit.
summary: This paper characterizes the dynamics of a quantum gas in a gravity-compensated shell trap, moving beyond simple harmonic approximations. By combining advanced theoretical tools like the Floquet expansion with experimental spectroscopy, the authors map the transition of the center-of-mass oscillation from harmonic to sound-wave-like behavior. This work is crucial for understanding quantum gas behavior in complex, curved potential geometries.
main_problem: The study investigates the center of mass oscillations of a quantum gas confined in a shell-shaped trap, focusing on the transition from simple harmonic motion to more complex, sound-wave-dominated dynamics as gravity compensation increases.
main_result: The analysis successfully derives and compares theoretical predictions, including beyond-RWA corrections via Floquet expansion, with experimental measurements, showing the transition to hydrodynamic behavior when gravity is nearly canceled.
method: The study employs both theoretical techniques, such as the Floquet expansion and deriving effective Hamiltonians, and experimental measurements involving resonant excitation spectroscopy of the center-of-mass motion.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum gas (e.g., Rb atoms) trapped in a shell-shaped trap using an rf-dressed quadrupole trap. The dynamics are modeled by analyzing the center-of-mass Hamiltonian, incorporating terms beyond the Rotating Wave Approximation (RWA).
key_observables: Center-of-mass oscillation frequency ($\omega_r$), damping rate, and the potential energy profile on the resonance surface.
important_parameters: Gravity sag ($\epsilon$), excitation amplitude ($d$), and the ratio of Rabi frequency to rf frequency ($\Omega_0/\omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on systematic expansions (Floquet expansion) and approximations (e.g., adiabatic approximation) to derive the effective Hamiltonian, which are the primary theoretical limitations.
figures_summary: Figures compare measured oscillation frequencies ($\omega_r$) against theoretical predictions derived from RWA and higher-order Floquet expansions, demonstrating frequency dependence on excitation amplitude and gradient.
paper_structure: The paper systematically builds the theoretical framework by first analyzing the trap potential using the Floquet expansion (beyond RWA) to derive an effective Hamiltonian. It then applies this to model the center-of-mass dynamics, comparing the resulting frequency predictions against experimental measurements across different physical regimes.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it bridges the gap between simple harmonic oscillator models and complex many-body hydrodynamics in ultracold atomic systems, providing quantitative insights into how trapping potentials and external forces modify fundamental quantum dynamics.
